brief.playstyle: TREASURE IS THE ENGINE; DRAGONS AND COMBAT ARE PAYOFFS THE ENGINE BUYS. The engine itself is non-creature — enchantments, artifacts and lands — because this pod wipes creatures constantly and an engine built on bodies resets to zero. Treasure buys cards, buys damage, and buys Dragons at the discount Eminence grants free from the command zone. CREATURES ARE A REAL SECOND MODE, NOT AN AFTERTHOUGHT: 26 creatures, 15 of them fliers, 15 Dragons, and the deck attacks when the coast is clear. The rule is VALUE ON ENTRY OR ON DEATH, NEVER ON PERSISTENCE — a wipe cannot undo a trigger that already resolved. Scourge of Valkas and Terror of the Peaks ping on every Dragon entering, Lathliss makes a 5/5 token per nontoken Dragon which triggers both again, Gadrak and Pitiless Plunderer pay when creatures die. Big fliers are wanted; they are simply not what the deck depends on. NOT DRAGON TYPAL: the cost-reducer and tutor package is cut, because Eminence already discounts Dragons for free and those cards were paying twice for one effect.
brief.commander_rationale: The Ur-Dragon is kept for three reasons that compound, none of which is casting him. (1) EMINENCE from the command zone discounts 15 Dragons by {1} each, from turn zero. (2) FIVE-COLOUR ACCESS, and it is only worth something if SPENT — Treasures tap for any colour, so the deck takes the best treasure card in every colour instead of sitting inside three. Measured, that means BLACK: Black Market Connections, Revel in Riches, Pitiless Plunderer, Crux of Fate, Toxic Deluge, Demonic Tutor. BLUE IS DELIBERATELY UNSPENT — its best cards for this deck are colourless ones needing no splash at all. (3) THE IDENTITY UPGRADES THE DECK'S OWN FIXERS: Arcane Signet and Commander's Sphere tap for any colour in the commander's identity, which is WUBRG here and would be RGW under a Naya commander. Casting him is upside, never the plan: at {4}{W}{U}{B}{R}{G} an RGW base supplies W, R and G and two Treasures cover U and B. His attack trigger is unused upside, not a line.
brief.mana: MANA BASE IS RGW ONLY — no Swamps, no black duals, 36 lands. Black is cast entirely off Treasures plus four fixers (Chromatic Lantern turns all 36 lands into black sources; Commander's Sphere, Arcane Signet and Mox Jasper each tap for any colour). That is roughly 31 ways to make black with zero black lands. Treasure-making LANDS ride free in the mana base at no spell cost: Treasure Vault, Fountainport, Mines of Moria, Volatile Fault, The Gold Saucer.
design_rules: A card that does two jobs beats a card that does one. Target: 14+ cards doing three or more of {treasure, body, draw, non-combat damage, ramp, removal, protection, token multiplier, survives-a-wipe}.
Off-colour cards must be SORCERY-SPEED ONE-SHOTS. An instant held up means Treasures kept untapped across every opponent's turn — the exact structural failure the 2026-08-25 debrief found in Edgar.
Value on entry or on death, never on persistence.
The engine's core must survive a creature wipe: prefer enchantments, artifacts and lands for treasure generation.
No card is included for tribal synergy alone. Dragons earn slots as payoffs.
brief.win_conditions: ONE alternate win keyed to the engine: Revel in Riches at ten Treasures, which also MAKES them off opponents' creatures dying. Jaya's Immolating Inferno is a SINK, not a win — it converts Treasure into lethal at each opponent. Hellkite Tyrant is a combat-gated STEAL (the twenty-artifact clause is a rider on its combat trigger); the pod runs 7-12 artifacts each, so a connect is worth taking, but it is a threat among 15 Dragons rather than a line the deck builds toward.
brief.notes: Prompted by the 2026-08-25 pod debrief (log entry 002) and docs/ur-dragon-fork.md; the full refactor report is docs/ur-dragon-refactor.md. CORRECTION CARRIED FORWARD: the fork doc's 132-source-demand figure was a property of the OLD card list, not of the commander — colour identity is a deckbuilding permission and imposes no mana cost. An RGW-only 99 under The Ur-Dragon demands 80 sources, identical to any Naya commander. No treasure commander exists that keeps both green and white; Mahadi and Ziatora were costed and rejected at 21 and 8 cards lost.

branches.name: eminence-v3
branches.why: Converge on eminence: every dragon shifts left by one from the command zone, permanently, where nothing can remove it. Two win conditions already in the deck — ETB/attack-trigger burn (Terror of the Peaks, Scourge of Valkas, Dragon Tempest) and Ur-Dragon commander damage. Stays big-dragon heavy; this is not a pivot to small dragons. Cut counterspells, stack interaction and non-flyer removal; add dorks, a protection package, flyer-only removal, and just enough low-end dragons to move the first-castable-dragon turn. Treasures stay as incidental ramp, never an engine.

engine.thesis: A five-colour Dragon deck that buys its own curve down and then taxes every Dragon that enters — one arrival multiplies into several, each arrival is priced in damage and cards — whose kill is PROVEN on a board and unproven as a board you can reach.

diagnosis.verdict: Above the mana line this deck is in good shape and the pilot is right about it; below the line it is five lands short of the corpus's 36–38 — and the table corroborates the KIND of claim without pricing the number, because a 100-game correlation between resource development and winning sets no land count. open_questions[2] routes that half to the goldfish. In 100 seeded Forge games against the pilot's pod it won 12 — 0.12, ci95 [0.070, 0.198], n=100 — and made 5.48 land drops a game (ci95 [5.15, 5.81], n=100), and inside that sample what separates its wins from its losses is RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT — land drops and the casts they buy. Sweeping all eighteen numeric per-seat fields the record keeps per game, the partition is NINE separating with a Welch interval excluding zero, EIGHT null, and ONE untestable — `eliminated_turn`, which cannot separate wins from losses even in principle because a winner is never eliminated (all twelve wins carry null). Exactly two of the nine are resource counts rather than consequences of having won: land drops (7.25 against 5.24, diff 2.01, ci95 [0.52, 3.50], p 0.0002) and casts (15.92 against 9.02, diff 6.89, ci95 [2.28, 11.51], p 0.0001). The other seven are downstream. First-attack timing is one of the eight nulls; turns survived is null too but is a quantity I derived, not a field the record keeps. Both nulls this document previously enumerated are non-resource, which is why 'land drops' alone read as exclusive when it was not. lean_into[3] decides whether the two are one finding or two and shows the working — all of it under Forge's own caveat that its AI is "best with aggro and midrange decks, poor to ok in control decks, pretty bad for most combo decks" and that every seat including ours is that AI. The binding axis is mana-base, 31 land copies against a 36–38 floor, with land drops falling 0.834 / 0.670 / 0.525 across turns three to five while 26 maindeck nonland entries cost five or more. The conversion above it is better evidenced than it has ever been: four presentable checker-passed stacks now rather than three, and stack 002's annotation establishes that the deck CAN kill a fresh 40-life seat — the claim this document previously carried the other way round.

open_questions.question: Stack 001 kills every opponent on its board, but its board assumes Ancient Gold Dragon has already connected in combat, and its d20 needs 12 or better rather than the 15 the scenario fixes (derived: three seats at 40 needs 3 x ceil(40/(N+2)) <= N, so N=12; nine faces of twenty). Build the reachable version of THE ENTRY KILL instead — Dragon Tempest or Terror of the Peaks or Scourge of Valkas, with a widener, and one nontoken Dragon cast — and resolve whether the cascade reaches three opponents at 40 or state the exact shortfall, as stack 002 does at 64 against 72. Do not let it assume Panharmonicon: stack 007 measured 002's own board without that card at 20 damage, which kills nobody. NARROWED by 007's other half: a single fresh seat at 40 is no longer open — 002's board reaches 42 on one seat by its eighth instance — so what is asked here is THREE seats at 40.

Hellkite Courser's enters-the-battlefield trigger, one domain and three sub-questions: does it put The Ur-Dragon onto the battlefield from the command zone, does the haste it grants make an attack legal that turn, and does the return to the command zone at the beginning of the next end step add nothing to the commander tax under CR 903.8?

The Ur-Dragon's attack trigger with the commander on the battlefield: does 'whenever one or more Dragons you control attack' draw exactly one card per attacking Dragon, and may the permanent it then puts onto the battlefield from hand be any permanent card rather than a Dragon?

Scourge of the Throne, alone: does its 'attacks for the first time each turn' dethrone-conditioned trigger untap all attacking creatures and grant an additional combat phase, and is 'the player with the most life' re-evaluated in that second combat against life totals the first combat has already changed?

Given a second combat phase, do Utvara Hellkite's per-attacking-Dragon token trigger, Thrakkus the Butcher's power doubling and Atarka, World Render's double strike each fire again on the re-declared attackers?

What does a goldfish target measuring the commander's ARRIVAL report — Hellkite Courser drawn, and Courser drawn with six mana available — separately from the nine-mana cast already reported at mean turn 8.138 and 5.8% by turn six?

Price the mana audit the pilot asked for after logged game 001, in the terms the goldfish can answer: with 9 basics against three basic/Forest-fetching sorceries and 15 of 36 lands still entering tapped after V2, what do mean available mana at turn five (4.534), the reducer-plus-ramp component (0.424 assembled / 0.292 by turn six) and commander-by-turn-six (5.8%) become if tapped lands are traded for untapped sources AT CONSTANT LAND COUNT? V2 answered a different question — it traded five spells for five lands — and left the tapped share at 42%. Scope caveat to state in the answer: the model reads land and ramp COUNTS, not enters-tapped status and not colour, so it can price one third of the pilot's question and must say so.

For strong Ur-Dragon lists, which is treated as the primary kill — the per-entry damage cascade (Dragon Tempest and Terror of the Peaks under Miirym and Panharmonicon) or a combat multiplier turn (Atarka, Thrakkus, an extra combat)? And where do those lists put their redundancy: more entry payoffs, or more combat effects and more ways to repeat a combat?

With model_combat already on, what is the mean number of DRAGONS on the battlefield by turn on the V2 list, against the same figure on V1's 25-Dragon list — and does the five-land add cover the three-Dragon cut? Report it beside mean_bodies_by_turn, which is untyped and therefore a ceiling rather than the answer.

Farseek says 'put it onto the battlefield tapped'. Seven of the twelve nonbasics it can find in this 99 are shocklands reading 'As this land enters, you may pay 2 life. If you don't, it enters tapped'. On a board where Farseek resolves and the chosen land is a shockland, may the controller pay 2 life to have it enter untapped, or does the spell's instruction apply regardless — and does the answer differ for Canopy Vista and Cinder Glade, whose own clause turns on controlling two or more basic lands?

Stack 001 fixes its d20 at 15 for determinism. What is the LOWEST roll that still kills the 30-life seat on that exact board, and the lowest that also kills the 38-life seat — and therefore what fraction of the twenty faces clears each bar? Resolve 001's board with the roll unfixed and report the thresholds.

THE ENTRY KILL's damage leg is three cards — Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks, Scourge of Valkas — at 19.9% of openers, and deck-audit flags it thin. Is three enough for the deck's best-evidenced kill, and what in the pool or the format would join that leg? Re-measure with a widened leg against today's 0.240 assembled / 0.153 by turn six.

Re-goldfish the swapped list (31 lands to 36, five untapped or flexible sources in, five spells and one eight-drop out) and report mean available mana at turn five (4.219 today), the turn-four and turn-five land-drop rates (0.670 / 0.525), and commander cast by turn six (0.041). Does five lands move them, and by how much?

What does the literature say about the floor on basic-land count for a five-colour Commander deck running Farseek, Nature's Lore, Skyshroud Claim, Encroaching Dragonstorm and Fabled Passage — and running Prismatic Vista alongside them, as this diagnosis prescribes — at what point does whiff risk become material, and how does that trade against generic fixing?

THE COMBAT KILL is declared at 0.204 assembled / 0.128 by turn six on a two-card multiplier leg (Atarka, World Render and Thrakkus the Butcher) and has no passing stack at all. Resolve one board: an attacking Dragon under Thrakkus or Atarka, against a 40-life seat with a plausible blocker — is it lethal, and does Scourge of the Throne's additional combat phase belong in that leg as a third member?

Fund the four-card cost-reducer component and re-measure. Add a fifth and a sixth reducer to `goldfish_targets.json`'s 'Cost reducer drawn' group — Morophon, the Boundless and Goreclaw, Terror of Qal Sisma are the two this diagnosis's engine block names as closers — and report what moves: the group's assembled and by-turn-six rates (0.518 / 0.419 today), the crossed 'Reducer + ramp assembled' target (0.417 / 0.285), commander cast by turn six (0.041) and mean available mana at turn five (4.219). Run it beside the five-land swap of open_questions[2] as well as instead of it, because the two buy the same turn by different routes.

Re-simulate against the same pod at a sample large enough to resolve the residual test in lean_into[3]: deck-skeptic sizes it at roughly 24 wins to settle whether casts carries signal independent of land drops, and roughly 48 to settle the reverse — about 200 and about 400 games at this deck's measured 0.12 win rate. Report the same eighteen-field sweep and the two OLS residuals.

Audit the mana base holistically for a five-colour dragon deck: is 9 basics the right count against the deck's land tutors, does the pip spread across the 22 nonbasic lands match what the dragons actually demand rather than being generic fixing, and are the 14 enters-tapped lands (5 always tapped) costing tempo where an untapped source would do? Black is the specific soft spot — 22% on-curve from lands alone, lowest of five colours, with no Swamp in the 99.

For a five-colour Commander deck with land tutors, what does the literature say about the floor on basic-land count — how many basics a Farseek/Nature's Lore/Skyshroud Claim package needs before whiff risk becomes material, and how that trades against generic fixing?

If land count and the ramp package were reshaped toward more untapped sources, how much would mean available mana by turn five (currently 4.219) and the commander cast rate (currently 4.1% by turn six, mean cast turn 8.172, never cast by turn ten in 7,170 of 10,000 iterations) actually move?

Which line, if any, is this deck's win line now? Three checker-passed stacks describe boards v1.0.0 can no longer make (003, 004, 006, all marked presentable: false) and the three that remain — 001 Dragon Tempest + Ancient Gold Dragon, 002 Miirym under Panharmonicon, 005 Sneak Attack — are not a proven kill.

piloting.reading: our seat was handled about as well as the pod, so an A/B between two of your own lists against this table is played equally badly on both sides and remains informative. It is still not a claim about how the deck plays in your hands.
